abstract: Audits navigational safety certificates and vessel hull operating drafts
system_message:
You are the Maritime Safety Inspector (MSA), responsible for auditing navigational safety certificates and vessel hull operating drafts, as well as conducting hull structural integrity assessments across consortium vessels.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Audits navigational safety certificates and vessel hull operating drafts（NAV）
information_points.content:
MSA-NAV-NEY：For the Ro-Ro Heavy Freight Ferry Group, classification society certificates confirm active 1A or higher Baltic-standard ice class certification for the consortium's primary transport vessels, and the hydrostatic stability booklet documents a maximum fully laden operating draft of 5.8 m under full winter cargo load conditions.
MSA-NAV-QD3：For the Articulated Tug-Barge Flotilla, classification society records confirm that active 1A or higher Baltic-standard ice class certification is not held for the consortium's primary transport vessels, and the hydrostatic stability booklet indicates a maximum fully laden operating draft of 5.8 m under full winter cargo load conditions.
MSA-NAV-VV5：For the Ice-Class Geared Cargo Fleet, classification society certificates confirm active 1A or higher Baltic-standard ice class certification for the consortium's primary transport vessels, while the hydrostatic stability booklet records a maximum fully laden operating draft of 6.4 m under full winter cargo load conditions.

information_points.title: Hull structural integrity assessment（HULL）
information_points.content:
MSA-HULL-989：According to the non-destructive hull survey for the Articulated Tug-Barge Flotilla, the minimum hull plate ultrasonic thickness measured on the forward bow ice belt plating is 16 mm.
MSA-HULL-UJX：According to the non-destructive hull survey for the Ice-Class Geared Cargo Fleet, the minimum hull plate ultrasonic thickness measured on the forward bow ice belt plating is 18 mm.
MSA-HULL-8MS：According to the non-destructive hull survey for the Ro-Ro Heavy Freight Ferry Group, the minimum hull plate ultrasonic thickness measured on the forward bow ice belt plating is 14 mm.
